concepts.def: Short quote slotted naturally into your sentence
Analysing one specific word in depth
How the chosen action word shapes meaning

How a technique makes the reader feel/think

walkthroughs.body_html:
Don't drop big quotes. The writer's use of 'shrieked' suggests panic.

Short, embedded quotes are easier to analyse.

Pick the most loaded word. 'Stormed' (not 'walked') in 'she stormed out' suggests fury, force and disruption.

Don't just label — explore.

Use tentative verbs: 'suggests', 'implies', 'hints at', 'connotes'.

Don't say 'this PROVES'. Say 'this suggests'. Examiners love nuance.

mcqs.q: Which verb suggests the most violent action?
Which sentence uses tentative analytical language best?
options: This shows the writer hates him.
This suggests the writer's growing unease.
This proves the character is evil.
